_comment: Pinned yt-dlp standalone binary vendored into the PyInstaller bundle.
Single source of truth: read by .github/workflows/release.yml AND
scripts/release_preflight.sh. ffmpeg's and alass's pins are duplicated across
those two files; do not repeat that here.
Every asset MUST be a standalone build. The bare 'yt-dlp' asset is a zipimport
archive whose shebang runs the system python3, so bundling it would make a
packaged app depend on a host Python it does not ship, and it carries no
curl_cffi (no impersonation). yt-dlp_macos is a universal2 binary, so one asset
serves both the arm64 and Intel macOS legs.
Digests are hardcoded rather than verified against the release's own
SHA2-256SUMS: that manifest is same-origin with the asset, which is exactly the
weaker property the alass steps avoid by pinning.
yt-dlp ships roughly monthly and dependabot cannot see a curl'd release URL, so
bumping this is a release-prep step. scripts/check_ytdlp_pin.py gates it: it
fails the build when this pin is definitively stale, and only warns when GitHub
is unreachable or rate-limited (a transient API failure must not block a release
under the never-tag-on-red rule).
To bump: set version, then for each asset run
gh release download <version> --repo yt-dlp/yt-dlp --pattern SHA2-256SUMS
and copy the matching lines.
